source_span: We estimate NVDA is generating ~$50-60B/Q in FCF - a big portion of which has been put back into the system, so this could easily take ~$50B or more out of the system - at least temporarily
source_chain: Jensen is the key driving force behind NVDA's financing of neo-clouds, LLM developers and suppliers, therefore a CEO change pauses that dealmaking in the near term, therefore roughly $50B or more of the ~$50-60B/Q FCF normally recycled into the system could be pulled out temporarily, worse because rates are rising and parts of the credit market are already illiquid (invalidation: a new leader who maintains the same approach limits this to a near-term pause, not a permanent withdrawal).
pulse_chain: UBS says Nvidia generates roughly $50B-$60B/Q in free cash flow, much of it recycled into financing for cloud providers, model developers and suppliers, therefore a pause under new leadership could pull $50B or more out of that system temporarily, worse while rates rise and parts of the credit market are thin.
why: The pulse reproduces UBS's exact figures, the financing-recycling mechanism, the CEO-change-causes-a-pause step, and the rates/illiquid-credit aggravating condition, attributed to the correct bank with no reversed or invented step.
